Let <MATH_0001> be a profinite topological group.
Then
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is torsion for <MATH_0003> and any <MATH_0004>-module <MATH_0005>, and
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0006> if <MATH_0007> is a <MATH_0008>-vector space.
<STRUCT_0004>

Proof of (1). By dimension shifting we see that it suffices
to show that <MATH_0001> is torsion for every <MATH_0002>-module <MATH_0003>.
Choose an exact sequence <MATH_0004> with <MATH_0005>
an injective object of the category of <MATH_0006>-modules.
Then any element of <MATH_0007> is the image of an element
<MATH_0008>. Choose <MATH_0009> mapping to <MATH_0010>.
The stabilizer <MATH_0011> of <MATH_0012> is open, hence
has finite index <MATH_0013>. Let <MATH_0014> be a system
of representatives for <MATH_0015>. Then <MATH_0016> is an invariant
element of <MATH_0017> which maps to <MATH_0018>. Thus <MATH_0019> kills the element
of <MATH_0020> we started with. Part (2) follows as then
<MATH_0021> is both a <MATH_0022>-vector space and torsion.
